title: Runtime: wire scheduler policy knobs through config system (per-pool + per-model defaults) with validation
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Internal only: adds validated config plumbing for mixed-workload scheduler knobs (per pool + per model), enabling safe canary ramps via runtime config without code deploys.
body:
## Summary This PR wires the mixed-workload scheduler policy knobs into the runtime config system so we can set sane defaults per model and override per pool during canary ramps. It includes validation, safe bounds, and a consistent precedence order. This is a prerequisite for the us-east canary plan where we need to tune thresholds/token budgets without redeploying runtime.

## Context The short/long prompt-aware scheduling prototype (two-queue + aging) introduced a handful of runtime flags. We currently have: (a) hard-coded defaults in runtime, (b) a couple of CLI/env toggles, and (c) ad-hoc per-pool overrides in the scheduler tests. That is not acceptable for production canary because it makes it too easy to set unsafe values and too hard to reason about what config is actually applied.

## What’s in this PR 1) Config schema + plumbing: - Adds `scheduler.policy.mixed_workload` config block to runtime config (control plane delivered). - Supports per-model defaults (by model ID / serving profile) and per-pool overrides (Hosted region pools + Dedicated pools). - Establishes precedence: pool override > model default > runtime baked-in default. - Adds explicit “unset” handling so we don’t accidentally override with zero-values.

2) Validation + safe bounds (server-side + runtime-side): - Validates on config ingestion (control plane) and also validates again at runtime load (defense-in-depth; protects against older control planes / manual config injection in Dedicated). - Rejects/auto-clamps clearly unsafe values and emits a structured warning log + metric `runtime_config_validation_failures_total{section="scheduler"}` when we have to fall back.

3) Knobs exposed (initial set): - `enabled` (bool): gates mixed-workload policy (still behind feature flag at rollout level). - `classification`:
  - `short_prompt_max_tokens` (int): threshold for “short” class classification.
  - `long_prompt_min_tokens` (int): optional hysteresis to avoid flip-flop when predicted tokens are noisy.
  - `use_predicted_prefill_cost` (bool): whether classification can use prefill cost predictor if available.
- `dispatch`:
  - `short_queue_weight` (float): target share for short class under contention.
  - `aging_half_life_ms` (int): controls how quickly long requests gain priority.
  - `max_consecutive_short_batches` (int): burst cap to reduce starvation risk.
- `token_budgets`:
  - `prefill_tokens_per_iter_short` / `prefill_tokens_per_iter_long` (int)
  - `decode_tokens_per_iter_short` / `decode_tokens_per_iter_long` (int)
- `guardrails`:
  - `max_skew_ratio` (float): hard cap on dispatch skew.
  - `min_long_dispatch_interval_ms` (int): ensures long queue makes progress even under constant short load.

4) Observability: - Adds `runtime_scheduler_config_applied{pool,model,knob}` debug dump (sampled) and a one-shot INFO log on config reload with a redacted summary of applied policy. - Adds `runtime_scheduler_policy_enabled{pool,model}` gauge.

## Defaults + bounds (initial) - `short_prompt_max_tokens`: default 256, bounds [32, 4096]. - `short_queue_weight`: default 0.75, bounds [0.5, 0.95]. - `aging_half_life_ms`: default 250, bounds [50, 5000]. - `max_consecutive_short_batches`: default 8, bounds [1, 64]. - Token budgets: defaults vary by SKU; for now we keep runtime defaults and allow config override with bounds [128, 16384] per-iter to prevent accidentally turning off batching or over-allocating per step.

## Testing - Unit tests: - Config precedence (pool > model > default). - Validation behavior (reject, clamp, fallback) including older config payloads missing fields. - Hot-reload: scheduler sees updated knobs without restart (existing runtime config reload mechanism).

- Manual: - Applied config verified in staging on `runtime-canary-us-east` pool with `short_queue_weight=0.8` and `aging_half_life_ms=200`; confirmed via log line `SchedulerPolicyConfig{...}` and Grafana gauge.

## Rollout notes - No behavior change unless the scheduler policy feature flag is enabled AND the config block is present (or runtime defaults apply). - This PR is intended to be merged ahead of the canary enablement ticket; config will be applied progressively with SRE guardrails.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR) - Add per-SKU defaults in control plane (right now SKU-specific defaults remain in runtime; see discussion with Hiro/Yuki re: kernel selection stability). - Extend validation to be aware of model max context / KV cache mode. - Docs update in internal runtime metrics/config guide (tracked separately).

## Review conversation (highlights) - Lena Fischer: “Can we avoid allowing `short_queue_weight < 0.5`? That seems like it can invert the goal.” Benji Okafor: “Agreed; set min=0.5 and added comment explaining why. Also added `max_skew_ratio` as a guardrail so even high weights can’t starve long.” - Sean Gallagher: “Need deterministic precedence and an audit trail of what was applied per pool.” Benji Okafor: “Added precedence tests + sampled metric/log dump. Also validation failures increment a counter so we can alert if config is flapping.” - Noah Patel: “Hot reload: ensure scheduler reads a snapshot not a partially updated struct.” Benji Okafor: “Switched to atomic pointer swap on config refresh and added a race test in `-race` suite.”

Approvals: - Sofia Ivanova: ✅ “Looks good; unblocks canary.” - Lena Fischer: ✅ “Knob set matches what we need; bounds are reasonable.” - Sean Gallagher: ✅ “SRE ok with validation + logging.”

## Merge Merged via squash into `main`.

runtime/scheduler: read policy knobs from runtime config snapshot (precedence + defaults)
runtime/config: add validation and clamping w/ metrics + warning logs
tests: add precedence + hot-reload + validation coverage
observability: add applied-config gauge + sampled dump
